verdict.rationale: Modal's Python SDK lets an agent request GPUs in code via the `gpu` argument and run workloads programmatically. An official CLI and an agent skill are documented, and containers spin down to zero automatically, which covers provisioning, execution and teardown without the console. Monitoring is only described as logs and metrics plus OpenTelemetry export, with no evidence that an agent can read them through the API or CLI. No MCP server or OpenAPI spec was found, and explicit teardown commands are not evidenced. missing for 10: documented programmatic or CLI access to GPU monitoring metrics, explicit teardown/stop commands, an MCP server or public OpenAPI spec, hands-on corroboration of an agent running the end-to-end flow.

support.subject: As an AI agent, I can provision a GPU, monitor it, run a workload, and tear it down end to end through documented APIs, CLI, or MCP without a human in the console

citations.quote: You can pick a specific GPU type for your Function via the `gpu` argument.
The [Modal](https://modal.com/) Python SDK allows you to deploy high-performance serverless applications and programmatically interact with the Modal platform.
Modal distributes an [official skill](./py/modal/skills/modal/SKILL.md) to help coding agents use its latest features.
In contrast, _Modal spins containers_ up and down in 1-2 seconds.
Comprehensive logs and metrics for every function and sandbox, down to the container.
